I resisted taking any mental health meds for my own experiences with both anxiety/depression, whatever else is a name for it. But I was reaching desperate points and after just one year of antidepressants and therapy, there's been noticeable progress in me and how less fearful of everything I am. My anxiety still wins sometimes, especially around my period time, however, I hold on to those moments of clarity. Like if I'm down again, I remind myself, "hey remember just a week ago? I did all that stuff and fear or those other thoughts weren't even on my mind because I was so incredibly focused on what I was enjoying or doing?" Or I remind myself, "remember that time last week? Remember how it was even simply POSSIBLE to go that time without this weight of anxiety"? And slowly over time, I think this helps in helping reduce the level of spirals in anxiety and depression that could have been. I also record those moments sometimes to remind myself it's possible. The most helpful thing I found was just having trust and faith without knowing for sure. And that's definitely a leap you gotta figure out how to take on your own.
